correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple G of order \(n\ge3\), the established two-colour wild identity equals \(2(n-1)-r(R)-r(B)\). The optimum over surjective colourings equals 2(n-1) minus the rank of the union of two graphic matroids, because two disjoint optimal forests can be colored oppositely and enlarged while retaining their ranks. The Edmonds–Nash-Williams union formula converts this to maximum partition deficiency exactly (both inequalities are explicitly proved). Binary cycle-space direct-sum dimensions show that upper value n-1 occurs precisely when all cycles are monochromatic, hence iff colour assignments are constant per edge block. An explicit one-edge red colouring attains n-2 when there is a single edge block. Surjective recolouring moves change the wild value by at most 1 and connect the colouring space when \(|E|\ge3\); the \(|E|=2\) connected case is treated separately. The claimed maximum-colouring multiplicity is \(2^{b(G)}-2\) for b>=2. Exhaustive finite corroboration independently checks 770 labelled connected graphs of orders 3–5 and five six-vertex examples, all their surjective colourings, deficiency endpoints and block multiplicity. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the combination of a sharp partition-deficiency minimum, an edge-block-sensitive maximum and multiplicity, and a full gap-free spectrum for every connected graph. The foundational 2025 paper proves the two-colour component identity but not this unrestricted spectrum; the full-text 2026 wild-number preprint proves an unrestricted spectrum for complete graphs and studies complete bipartite graphs and other restricted colourings. A prior specific complete-bipartite-spectrum result is strictly a special case, not an implication in the reverse direction. Classical matroid union directly gives the minimum upon translating ranks and is credited; it does not by itself establish upper endpoint/multiplicity or the full interval. No equivalent all-graph full-spectrum and block-multiplicity theorem was found in the actually inspected sources or search results. Bibliographic completeness, particularly under matroid-connectivity language, is not guaranteed.
residual_risks: The total-graph interval and block-maximum synthesis may exist under the graphic matroid connectivity function (or equivalent branchwidth/connectedness) terminology in sources not surfaced in the searches.
The matroid-union part of the result is an established implication and carries no separate novelty credit.

value.rationale: A full classification for every connected graph supplies the exact best and worst shared-edge upgrade counts and proves every intermediate requirement attainable. The sharp best-end formula identifies arbitrary multiway partition bottlenecks; the worst-end formula and \(2^{b(G)}-2\) count identify the structural role of articulation, bridges, and biconnected blocks. This addresses a naturally studied graph invariant introduced in 2025 and investigated for special families in 2026; it subsumes complete-graph, tree, cycle and complete-bipartite cases without excluding sparse or cut-vertex networks. Even though essential mathematical tools are classical and simple, the complete all-graph attainment theorem and structural multiplicity are motivated and useful as a unified classification, not a renamed single-parameter formula.
